answer.says: Ramesh, the wages are due, and the kitchen is closed. I have only three hundred and forty-six rupees in my pocket, but I will pay what I can. The rest is a debt I acknowledge, though the state that should employ me has misfiled my name. For now, I must live on the credit of my own word and the patience of the man who keeps my house.
answer.thought: The body is tired from the walk, and the hunger is a dull ache that no amount of chai can fully satisfy. I have little cash, but dignity in a household is bought with punctuality, even if the rest is written off as a debt to be settled when the bureaucracy corrects its error. I will pay Ramesh what I have, leaving him the balance as a promise, and then sit in the darkening room to think.
